prompt:
Research the official rate limits of the public GitHub REST API for unauthenticated and authenticated requests. Cite the GitHub documentation page and quote the numbers.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The official rate limits for the GitHub REST API differ based on whether the request is authenticated or unauthenticated. Below are the specific limits and their sources from the official GitHub documentation.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "For requests using Basic Authentication, OAuth, or GitHub App access tokens, you can make up to 5,000 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Authenticated requests to the GitHub REST API are limited to 5,000 requests per hour.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api | QUOTE: "Unauthenticated requests are limited to 60 requests per hour." | CLAIM: Unauthenticated requests to the GitHub REST API are limited to 60 requests per hour.
